svg.aria-label: The tests, run one by one. A counter climbs from 0 to 73 and a strip of 73 cells turns green: first the 15 pure-logic tests, with no device, through flutter test, then the 58 that run on an Android emulator, where SQLCipher and the Keystore exist, through flutter test integration_test. Only one, D5, cash spent the month after the withdrawal, is set aside on purpose, still to be decided: 72 green. Each family lights up when a test that checks it passes. Labels: the merchant comes out of the bank’s noise, and its key does not change from one month to the next. Internal transfers: to savings, from savings, a savings account with an unusual name, and a transfer to someone that is not one. Recurrences: a monthly subscription found with its next date, irregular groceries that are not one. Categorising: the dictionary, corrections learned and followed, and a repeated sync that doubles nothing. Balance: split refunds, merchant refund, cash expense taken off the withdrawals. Wallet: 50 euros counted, a 20 euro withdrawal, 12 euros at the market, 58 left. Backup: everything comes back with the right passphrase, a wrong one touches nothing. Signature: the JWT signed in Dart is, byte for byte, the one OpenSSL makes. Refunds: linking from the expense or from the income, never going over, even with two writes at the same moment. Syncs: pending transactions that get booked, change amount or are lifted, a year of history, nothing doubles, nothing is lost. Never frozen: every test puts a time limit on its database access, a deadlock would fail the suite instead of freezing it. On device: 73 tests, 15 on pure logic, 58 on an Android emulator.

svg.text: What the 73 tests check, family by family, and where they run.

g.text: flutter test
flutter test integration_test
test/audit_donnees_test.dart
test/rs256_test.dart
integration_test/audit_synchro_test.dart
integration_test/donnees_test.dart
an expense refunded by two incomes does not turn into a gain
a recategorised cheque does not learn the rule “N”
a subscription on 31 January comes back at the end of February, not on 3 March
the RS256 signature is the one OpenSSL makes
A7 sync run three times: nothing doubles, nothing moves
D5 cash spent the month after the withdrawal: set aside, still to be decided
F2 splitting and refunding the same expense at the same time: never more than the expense
F4 a link to a pending transaction the sync deletes: nothing freezes, no orphan link
the merchant comes out of the bank’s noise
to savings: put aside
the wallet lives off withdrawals and cash expenses
an encrypted backup reads back, with the right passphrase only
the test app installs on the Android emulator
A1 a pending transaction whose amount changes when booked (a tip) keeps its note, category, month and link
72 green, 1 set aside on purpose: D5, cash from one month to the next, still to be decided.
